about.title: Paramount Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Paramount's mix of industrial yards, distribution centers, and small manufacturing shops near corridors like Alondra Boulevard and Downey Avenue means workplace injuries here often involve heavy equipment, delivery trucks, or contractor crews. Under California law, workers' compensation is generally the only path against your employer regardless of who caused the accident, but that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to what happened, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. Our team reviews the details of your situation, explains your options, and helps you understand what deadlines apply. There's no cost for a consultation, and no obligation to move forward if you're not ready.

whyChoose.title: Why You Should Talk to an Attorney First

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer in most cases, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be pursued separately.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline, so waiting can limit your options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing you for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and we can help you understand what protections apply to your situation.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse near Rosecrans Avenue. Can I still file a claim if I already reported it late?
items.answer: California generally asks that you report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, but missing that window doesn't automatically end your options. We can review the specific timeline and circumstances to see what's still available to you. There's no cost to have that conversation.

items.question: My employer says workers' comp covers everything. Is that true?
items.answer: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault, so in most cases that's correct as far as your employer goes. But if a third party, like a subcontractor, delivery driver, or equipment manufacturer, contributed to your injury, you may be able to pursue a separate claim against them. We can help sort out whether that applies to you.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim in Paramount?
items.answer: No, California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you believe that's happening, it's worth speaking with us about your rights. Contact us at no cost to discuss your situation.
